correctness.rationale: For odd distinct p=q+1. Substitution into mod q-1 yields q-1 | (p+1)(p+d), but multiplication by d can lose invertibility; theorem correctly retains the independent original condition q-1 | pr+1. Hence q<=1+(p+1)(2p-1)=2p²+p and r<=pq+2, finite p fiber. Converse checks all original divisibilities, no logical gap. Independently exhaustively enumerated odd primes q,r through the *proved* bounds for p=3,5, exactly obtaining p3 (3,5,17),(3,17,53), p5 (5,7,13),(5,7,37),(5,13,67),(5,19,97),(5,43,109). These tests do not substitute for the unrestricted algebraic bound. No statement on non-squarefree or four-prime products.

value.rationale: The fixed-least-prime finiteness theorem and explicit finite divisor sieve address a natural shifted Korselt three-prime classification, where the sign of the shift matters. Beyond rewriting the defining condition, the bound q<=2p²+p and complete first p fibers give a finite exact procedure for every p, potentially useful for further classification and testing conjectural prime-support patterns. No unsupported claim of an overall finite or infinite set of solutions is made.

limitations: Three distinct odd primes; each least-p fiber is finite, but global population and four-prime/non-squarefree cases unresolved.
